title: Motivation record (category or specific)
description: One record from motivations.json. The registry holds TWO record shapes under one declared schema — `categories` (a motivation group, which owns a list of specific ids) and `specifics` (a single motivation, which points back at its category). They are distinguished by their required fields, not by a discriminator key, so `oneOf` is exact here: a category carries `specific_ids` and no `category_source_key`; a specific carries `category_source_key` and no `specific_ids`. A malformed record satisfies neither branch and fails.
$comment: B-264: motivations.json declared this schema from the day it was generated (build_motivations.py:97) and the file did not exist, so the registry validated against NOTHING. Written from the shipped data — 32 categories, 283 specifics, field frequencies measured at 32/32 and 283/283, so every `required` below is a field that is present on every record rather than one that seemed likely.

oneOf.title: category

specific_ids.$comment: May be empty: `counts.categories_with_no_specifics` exists precisely to track that case, so an empty list is legal data and not a defect.

description.$comment: R-MDS-1: OPTIONAL authored prose, CATEGORIES ONLY. Absence stays legal — specifics carry none and a category may be written later. The prose is AUTHORED in mechanics voice (R-C2C-1, `motivation-sourcing-pass-gate` A2 term 3); it is never transcribed from a rulebook or from OggDude's hand-typed DataCustom file, which serves as reference beside the corpus and not as a source of shipped words.

source.$comment: A books.vocab.json KEY, not a display title. The validator resolves it (L1mo.desc_cited); the schema only requires that it be a non-empty string, because cross-registry resolution is the validator's job and not the schema's — the same division this file already draws for `category_source_key`.

section.$comment: The section as the book's own contents page names it. This is what makes a citation checkable WITHOUT a page number, which is the whole reason a null page is tolerable below.

page.$comment: The PRINTED page, or null. NULL IS AN HONEST STATE, not a gap to be filled in later by guesswork: corpus page != printed page (measured drift 1-3 across these books) and Docs/pdf_sources.json calibrates `page_offset` for `aor` alone, so most offsets cannot be computed. A book in B-334's TOC-blind class cannot even be TOC-judged. Null here means 'not yet render-and-read'; an integer means someone looked at the page. A wrong integer is worse than a null.

description_cite.$comment: R-MDS-1: the structured cite. Required whenever `description` is present — see `dependencies`.

oneOf.$comment: A category may carry authored prose. R-MDS-1: `description` and `description_cite` are both OPTIONAL, but a description WITHOUT a cite is INVALID — that is the `dependencies` clause below, and it is the schema-level half of the rule whose validator half is L1mo.desc_cited. The pairing is the point: unsourced prose in a registry is exactly the failure `c15-motivation-ingestion-home` refused when it kept the source's placeholder stubs out. BOTH SPELLINGS ARE PRESENT ON PURPOSE. This file declares $schema draft-07, where the keyword is `dependencies`; but `validate_registries.py` runs a Draft202012Validator, and 2020-12 REMOVED `dependencies` in favour of `dependentRequired`. A draft-07-only clause is therefore silently INERT under the validator that actually runs — which is how the first version of this rule passed a record carrying a description and no cite. Keeping both spellings makes the rule bind whichever validator reads the file, and the bite at the gate is what proved it was not binding before.

category_source_key.$comment: Points at a category by its display NAME (e.g. "Ambition"), not by id or _source_key — measured, not assumed. Left as a string here; the cross-reference is the validator's job, not the schema's.

category_rolls.title: category_rolls (top-level table, R-MRR-2)
category_rolls.$comment: NOT a record: the registry's top-level, LINE-keyed category roll table (ruling motivation-roll-ranges R-MRR-2). Validated by validate_registries L1mo.rolls against this $def; absent-tolerant — a registry without the block is legal for old readers, and the arm says so explicitly rather than passing silently. Bands carry category IDs (B-393's lesson); the validator resolves them and pins each line's three to the categories whose `sources` name that line's core book.

ten.$comment: the book's 10-cell, recorded; the app's behaviour is Amendment 2's reroll
